orphanHoldResidual.evidence: `Game1.player.animateOnce(279 + facing)` (Crop.cs:540) raises the animation pause through Farmer.animateOnce -> FarmerSprite.animateOnce (Farmer.cs:6479, FarmerSprite.cs:673) in another type, which this analysis' same-file callee walk cannot follow
the grab branch of the same harvest: `animateOnce(283 + facing)` on the same primitive, one frame later than the row above

only reachable from the `Event.playerControlSequence` setter, i.e. inside a running event; `Game1.eventUp = true` is set by the event driver (GameLocation.cs:15759-15766) in another file, and the body is given back by `setUpPlayerControlSequence` (Event.cs:11468)
orphanHoldResidual.bound: until the event releases the player control sequence

orphanHoldResidual.evidence: the engine's own single-animation hold primitive: it calls `FarmerSprite.animateOnce(...)` (Farmer.cs:6479) which raises the pause flag in FarmerSprite.cs, so the establishing write is in the callee's own type

the guard above requires every other declared fact to be ABSENT (`!Game1.eventUp && !UsingTool && ... && CanMove`), then takes the body and arms a 1000 ms + 1 ms frame pair; the only `PauseForSingleAnimation` write in this method CLEARS the flag, which is why this row is not accompanied
`CanMove = false` then `animateOnce(64/72/80/88, 50f, 8)`; the animation pause is raised through FarmerSprite in another type, so no same-file callee establishes it here

`who.canMove = false` then a one-frame 2000 ms animation whose frame-end behaviour IS the release (`Farmer.canMoveNow`, Object.cs:3315-3318); `Game1.pauseThenMessage` only arms `messageAfterPause`, which no declared read observes

orphanHoldResidual.unknownReason: the release is owned by a per-location `NetMutex`, and `RequestLock` is not where it runs: `lockRequest.Fire` (NetMutex.cs:56) polls itself synchronously (AbstractNetEvent1.cs:43-50), but the handler it fires claims the lock only on the MASTER (NetMutex.cs:34-41), so the two callbacks stored at :57-58 run from `NetMutex.Update` (:86-98) and only when `owner` changes. As the master that is still the same frame - `Game1.Update` runs `UpdateControlInput` (Game1.cs:4288) before `UpdateLocations` (:4315) - so `canMove` is false only inside the frame that re-trues it and no declared read can see it; as a REMOTE farmhand `owner` stays -1 until the host's grant arrives, so the body is held for a network round trip, and for as long as the host never grants it
orphanHoldResidual.settledBy: a live probe on the perch in the farmhand topology recording per tick `upgradeMutex.IsLockHeld()`, `player.CanMove` and the declared facts: it settles whether any tick has `CanMove == false` with every fact false, and how long that window lasts. If one does, the fact owed is a C# lane item - the body flag itself (`Farmer.CanMove`, which `WorldModel.DescribeNavigationHold` already publishes as `unknown_holder:CanMove` with `next_step=observe_again`, WorldModel.cs:514-525, :540-545), or `upgradeMutex.IsLockHeld()`, which is not actor-scoped and so is not a fact about the body
orphanHoldResidual.bound: one mutex update after the grant: inside a single frame as the master, at least one network round trip as a remote farmhand, unbounded if the grant never comes

orphanHoldResidual.evidence: this is the WARP's fade, not the global one: it CLEARS `globalFade` (ScreenFade.cs:82) and raises `fadeToBlack`, so the only fact up across it is `Game1.isWarping`, raised by `performWarpFarmer` (Game1.cs:10031) in another file

a `BaseFarmEvent`: the driver is the new-day sequence (`if (farmEvent != null && farmEvent.setUp())`, Game1.cs:8604) and its own tick (Game1.cs:4187-4193). Farm events run with `eventUp == false` - the two are tracked separately - so `DayTransition` is the fact, and `ActorWorldFacts` reads it as `newDay || farmEvent != null`
the same class and the same driver as the row above: a `BaseFarmEvent` mounted for the night

re-asserted every tick while the bus drives (`drivingBack || drivingOff`, BusStop.cs:309-323); the fact is `Game1.freezeControls`, raised where the ride starts (BusStop.cs:268) rather than in this method

the very next statement is `Game1.multipleDialogues(...)` (ManorHouse.cs:47-51), which mounts the box and sets `dialogueUp = true` (Game1.cs:9557-9562) in another file - the cross-file companion this analysis' same-file callee walk cannot see

`Game1.globalFadeToBlack(afterFall, 0.045f)` (MineShaft.cs:3024) raises `globalFade` inside ScreenFade, then this line takes the body; between the two the only fact up is the fade, and `afterFall` (:3037-3045) opens a dialogue before the mine re-entry
orphanHoldResidual.bound: the fade plus the fall dialogue
